subject: Re: Follow-up & test plan — reranking / embeddings comparison vs hyperscalers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@searchlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + proposed rerank/emb test plan

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great to learn more about SearchLytics' reranking use case and the latency sensitivity for production search (P95 target ~120ms). As promised, I put together a short test plan to compare Redwood vs the hyperscalers you mentioned (AWS Bedrock + OpenAI embeddings pipeline) focused on the metrics that matter for your team: retrieval latency, recall@k, and per-query cost for vector dims.

Proposed quick test (summary):
- Dataset: the 10k QA + passage set you shared (sample attached: rerank-test-queryset-10k.jsonl)
- Tests:
  1) Embeddings comparison: 768 vs 1536 dims (matching your current vector DB configs) — measure avg embed time, index build time, and per-embed unit cost.
  2) Retrieval + reranking pipeline: recall@1/5/10, MRR, and end-to-end P50/P95 retrieval + rerank latency.
  3) Cost estimate: tokens/embeds per query and projected monthly cost at your 10M qpm/month expected volume.
- Targets: recall@10 >= 0.85 (baseline), end-to-end P95 <= 120ms for the lowest-latency path, and per-query vector cost that meets your unit economics.

What we need from you: a short list of 200-500 representative queries (if you prefer not to share prod data we can run against synthetic + your sample) and confirmation which vector dims you'd like us to include (768, 1536).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Redwood runs a side-by-side run against your sample on our hosted env (shared API key) and on a dedicated node if you want network-isolated throughput numbers.
2) We schedule a 30-min sync with Aditya to walk through the test harness and accelerate onboarding.

Attaching the suggested benchmark spreadsheet and the sample queryset. I can also include a draft quote if you want to move to a short POC reserved window.

Would Monday 5/11 10:00am PT work for a quick sync?

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-rerank-benchmark-20260509.xlsx, rerank-test-queryset-10k.jsonl

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Samir Gupta <samir@searchlytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + proposed rerank/emb test plan — technical details

Hi team —

Quick technical note ahead of the call:
- Endpoints we'll use: /v1/embeddings (Redwood-provided model: redwood-embed-1536-v1 and redwood-embed-768-v1) and our rerank service that performs ANN recall + model re-rank.
- Indexing: we'll build FAISSIVF and HNSW variants to show tradeoffs (latency vs recall).
- Measurement: recall@1/5/10, MRR, index build time, memory footprint, and end-to-end P50/P95 for retrieval + rerank.
- Cost calc: embed cost per 1k vectors (we'll show multiple tiers), plus projected storage and query cost at your 10M/month volume.

Bench notes / expectations vs hyperscalers:
- Latency: with dedicated pool + KV caching we expect P95 retrieval+rerank to be ~80–140ms depending on index and dims (HNSW with 1536 will be slower but higher recall).
- Recall: we expect to match or exceed Bedrock/OpenAI pipeline recall@10 for comparable dims because of our rerank model and query-side caching.
- Cost: per-vector cost will typically be lower than hosted hyperscalers at scale due to batching and quantization-friendly runtime; we'll provide concrete per-query numbers.

Prep for the run: please share the query file and let us know if you have a preferred ground-truth mapping (doc ids for relevance). If not, we'll run a small manual eval set and flag the items we need human labels for.

Thanks — Aditya
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
